score.name: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, S.A.B. de C.V. (Pacific Airport Group)
score.moat_justification: Regulated local-monopoly airport concessions: GAP is the sole operator of 12 Mexican airports (Guadalajara, Tijuana, Puerto Vallarta, Los Cabos and 8 others) under 50-year concessions to 2048 plus 2 Jamaican airports, with maximum tariffs reset every five years under the Master Development Program framework and adjusted for Mexican PPI. Returns prove the franchise: fundamentals.json roic_proxy was 13.5% (FY2015), 26.4% (FY2018), 30.1% (FY2019), still 17.8% in the COVID trough (FY2020), 42.1% (FY2021), 64.8% (FY2022), 49.5% (FY2023) and 37.7% (FY2024) — above the cost of capital through a full cycle including a traffic collapse; ROE ran 36-46% in FY2022-24 and the ex-IFRIC-12 EBITDA margin was 67.1% in 2Q25 company reporting. Gross margin is not presented in the filing (no cost-of-sales split), so the moat rests on ROIC/ROE and margin evidence instead. Capped at 7, not higher: the concessions are finite (Mexican concessions expire 2048 and assets revert), the regulator sets the tariff ceiling and the mandated capex program (Ps.43,185m committed for the Mexican airports in the 2025-2029 MDP), traffic is cyclical, and earnings are MXN-denominated. CAP = 2 + 1.3 x 7 = 11.1 years.

moat_for: Sole-operator concessions: 12 Mexican airports (Guadalajara, Tijuana, Puerto Vallarta, Los Cabos + 8) to 2048 and 2 Jamaican airports — no competing airport in each catchment
Regulated pricing power proven in the 2025-2029 tariff reset: weighted average maximum tariffs +18.1% in 2025, with PPI indexation inside each five-year MDP period
ROIC well above the cost of capital through a cycle: roic_proxy 17.8% even in COVID-year FY2020, 49.5% FY2023, 37.7% FY2024 (fundamentals.json); ROE 36-46% FY2022-24
High and stable cash margins: EBITDA margin ex-IFRIC-12 67.1% in 2Q25 (66.8% 2Q24) in company reporting
Non-aeronautical diversification (retail, cargo/bonded warehouses via GWTC consolidated Jul 2024) growing faster than aeronautical and less traffic-sensitive
moat_against: Finite concessions: Mexican concessions expire 2048 (~22 years) and concession assets revert — a perpetuity terminal value assumes renewal the filing does not grant

Regulator sets the ceiling: five-year MDP reviews reset maximum tariffs and impose the capex program (Ps.43,185m committed 2025-2029 in Mexico); the 2025-2029 bases added a claw-back on excess workload units
Traffic cyclicality: Mexican workload units fell in 2024 (-1.7%) after +10.5% in 2023, and FY2020 revenue fell ~27% in MXN on COVID
MXN earnings vs a USD ADS price: the peso fell ~18% against the USD at the 2024 period-end ECB rate vs 2023, mechanically cutting USD owner's earnings
Mandatory MDP capex is the owner's-earnings story: the purchases-of-concession-assets line jumped to Ps.12,397m in FY2025, cutting filing-basis OE/share ~34% in MXN in one year

# PAC — Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacífico, S.A.B. de C.V. (Pacific Airport Group)

v5.4 pass-1 run, 2026-10-18. All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json / financials_history.csv / fundamentals.json, or quoted from the cited 20-F filings — none are recomputed. Where a figure is arithmetic on two cited filing lines it is labelled as such (the CX precedent in this sweep).

**Scope note:** PAC sits in the under-$40B queue on the universe screener's real market cap — 50,527,746 ADS (505,277,464 ordinary shares ÷ 10 per ADS) × $203.90 ≈ $10.3B. The engine's market_cap_est prints $103.03B because it multiplies the per-ADS price by the ordinary share count (the standing ADS artifact in this system — same as JD/CHT/TS); judgment.json therefore carries in_scope_under_40b: false, which records the engine figure, not the economic one. The company is in scope; the artifact is disclosed here and should not be read as a $103B market cap.

## What it is
Operator of 14 airports under long-term concessions: 12 in Mexico's Pacific region (Guadalajara, Tijuana, Puerto Vallarta, San José del Cabo/Los Cabos, Bajío, Hermosillo, Mexicali, Los Mochis, La Paz, Manzanillo, Morelia, Aguascalientes) under 50-year concessions to 2048, and 2 in Jamaica (Montego Bay since 2015, Kingston since 2019). Revenue is aeronautical (regulated passenger/workload fees), non-aeronautical (retail, parking, cargo — including the Guadalajara World Trade Center bonded-warehouse business consolidated July 2024), plus IFRIC-12 construction revenue on concession improvements (a zero-margin pass-through: Ps.6,832,541 thousand of FY2024's Ps.33,614,374 thousand total revenue in the FY2025 20-F's selected-data table). Maximum tariffs and the mandated investment program are set in five-year Master Development Program (MDP) reviews; tariffs are adjusted for Mexican PPI inside each period. The 2025–2029 review raised weighted average maximum tariffs 18.1% in 2025 and committed Ps.43,185 million of investment at the Mexican airports over the period (company reporting / FY2025 20-F).

## Owner's earnings
The preliminary engine run exited 4 with DATA_GAP: sbc, capex, shares — no tier. All three gaps were resolved inside the bounded override authority (kind "filing" each; full sources in judgment.json and the OVERRIDE_APPLIED flags):

- **Capex:** companyfacts carries no capex concept for this filer at all — the filer's capex is the single combined cash-flow line "Purchases of machinery, equipment, improvements on leased assets, improvements to concession assets and advance payments to suppliers" (FY2024 20-F, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows): Ps.8,431,106 thousand (FY2022), Ps.10,444,346 thousand (FY2023), Ps.7,844,983 thousand (FY2024). The override declares the FY2023 value, Ps.10,444,346,000, because FY2023 is the median year of the normalized base once capex is charged at filed values — filing-leg OE/share (OCF from financials_history.csv minus each year's own filed capex, ÷ filed shares, ×10 per ADS) is $4.11 (FY2022), $4.08 (FY2023), $8.43 (FY2024) per ADS, so the scored base is built from the exact filed figure for its year. The single value overstates FY2024 capex and is charged to every earlier history year in 2023 pesos, which makes the pre-2021 history OE negative in financials_history.csv — an override artifact, disclosed, not a business fact (the company's MDP capex in those years was far smaller in nominal terms). FY2025's filed line is Ps.12,396,949 thousand: the new MDP cycle spends MORE, so the override does not flatter the forward picture.
- **SBC = Ps.0:** no equity compensation plans exist (FY2025 20-F Item 16G: "No equity-compensation plans have been approved by our shareholders"); Note 22 Employee Cost is entirely cash compensation, already inside OCF. Same treatment as TS/SQM/KEP/LTM in this sweep.
- **Shares = 505,277,464:** companyfacts carries WeightedAverageShares scaled 1,000× (505,277,464,000) — the share-basis defect family (NTNX/VIV/DD). The FY2025 20-F EPS disclosure prints weighted average shares of 505,277,464 for FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 (508,371,309 for FY2022) and states the company has no potentially dilutive shares, so basic = diluted. Cross-check from filed facts: FY2024 attributable profit Ps.8,612,157 thousand ÷ diluted EPS Ps.17.0444 = 505.28 million shares.
- **ADS ratio 10:** FY2025 20-F — each ADS represents 10 Series B shares; engine per-share figures are scaled ×10 to per-ADS.

Engine history (USD, FX-converted at period-end rates; capex at the override value, SBC 0):
- FY2022: OCF $640,257,765; OE $106,133,910 → $2.10/ADS
- FY2023: OCF $822,435,083; OE $206,009,782 → $4.08/ADS
- FY2024: OCF $803,869,931; OE $300,348,011 → $5.94/ADS (on the override's FY2023 capex; on FY2024's own filed capex the filing-leg figure is $8.43/ADS — FY2024 was the trough-capex year at the end of the 2020–2024 MDP)
- **Base used = normalized (median of last 3 FY) OE/share $4.0772 per ADS** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). OE yield at $203.90: 2.0%.
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC) prints $511,763,190 for FY2024 in financials_history.csv (per ADS ≈ $10.13 by the same filing-leg arithmetic) — it treats every peso of capex above D&A as growth. For a concession, MDP spend is the price of keeping the franchise's traffic capacity, so the conservative version is the right base; the maintenance figure is the upper edge of the method range and still yields only ~5.0% at the price.
- Net debt (engine, FY2024): $222,736,467 — 0.11× normalized OE (diagnostics). Balance sheet is not the problem; the price is.
- FY2025 evidence (filing only — companyfacts has not ingested the FY2025 20-F, see STALE_FY): OCF Ps.18,249,740 thousand, capex line Ps.12,396,949 thousand, so filing-leg OE ≈ Ps.5,852,791 thousand = Ps.115.85 per ADS — down ~34% in MXN from FY2024's filed-capex basis (Ps.174.75 per ADS) as the 2025–2029 MDP spend ramped. Near-term OE is capex-depressed by design of the regulatory cycle.

## MOAT: 7/10 — strong regulated concession monopoly, finite life
- FOR: sole-operator concessions — 12 Mexican airports to 2048 and 2 Jamaican airports, no competing airport in any catchment; regulated pricing power proven in the 2025–2029 reset (maximum tariffs +18.1% in 2025, PPI indexation inside the period); ROIC well above the cost of capital through a cycle — fundamentals.json roic_proxy 13.5% (FY2015), 26.4% (FY2018), 30.1% (FY2019), 17.8% in the COVID trough (FY2020), 42.1% (FY2021), 64.8% (FY2022), 49.5% (FY2023), 37.7% (FY2024), ROE 36–46% FY2022–24; EBITDA margin ex-IFRIC-12 67.1% in 2Q25 company reporting (66.8% 2Q24); non-aeronautical revenue growing faster than aeronautical and less traffic-sensitive.
- AGAINST: finite concessions — Mexican concessions expire 2048 and assets revert, so the model's perpetuity terminal value assumes a renewal no filing grants; the regulator sets both the tariff ceiling and the mandated capex (Ps.43,185m committed 2025–2029; the new bases add a claw-back on excess workload units); traffic cyclicality (Mexican workload units +10.5% in 2023, −1.7% in 2024, +3.7% in 2025 per the FY2025 20-F); MXN earnings against a USD price (the 2024 period-end ECB rate was ~18% below 2023's, mechanically cutting USD OE); gross margin is not presented in the filing (no cost-of-sales split), so the moat case rests on ROIC/ROE and the EBITDA margin, not on a gross-margin series.
- A 7 gives CAP = 11.1 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 11.1 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — v5.4 final run (2026-10-18)
Growth recalibration (written reason, required by the sanity check): the engine blend is 16.92%, but its components do not describe repeatable growth — OE/share CAGR 2y is +68.16%, a capex-cycle artifact (FY2022 charged at peak capex under the single-value override, FY2024 an MDP-trough year); the revenue CAGRs (5y 13.53%, 3y 20.30%) are inflated by IFRIC-12 construction revenue and, in USD, by FX swings (latest USD revenue YoY −17.36% vs +1.2% in MXN); and the one genuinely large recent print — FY2025 MXN revenue +23.2% — is a one-time tariff step (+18.1%) plus the GWTC consolidation, not an annual rate. Underlying drivers are passenger traffic (+3.7% in 2025) plus PPI tariff indexation. Scenario starts were therefore set via offsets (−0.21/−0.14/−0.09/−0.04/+0.03 vs the blend) to −4.1 / +2.9 / **+7.9** / +12.9 / +19.9%. Probabilities skewed bear-ward (15/25/30/20/10 vs the 10/25/30/25/10 default) on OE_VOLATILE, the FY2025 capex ramp already in evidence, and FX; OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $203.90 (nasdaq_quote_api).

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | −4.1% | 0.75 | $18.42 | 3.48% |
| Bear | 25% | 2.9% | 0.90 | $30.69 | 4.39% |
| Base | 30% | 7.9% | 1.00 | $43.20 | 5.36% |
| Bull | 20% | 12.9% | 1.10 | $60.26 | 6.66% |
| Super bull | 10% | 19.9% | 1.25 | $95.51 | 9.12% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $45.00 (−77.9% vs price), IV@12% $60.83, weighted IRR 5.56%, base-case IRR 5.36%. Hurdle prices: IV@20% $30.98, IV@25% $23.40.**
- **Tier by numbers: D. Band D → D** (bear and bull cases are both Tier D — there is no plausible-end disagreement about this verdict).
- Diagnostics: OE yield 2.00%, terminal value 20.6% of IV@15%, scenario spread 5.18×, net debt 0.11× normalized OE, 21.6 months since FY end (engine basis).
- Robustness check on the un-recalibrated defaults: with the engine's own starts (base 16.9%, super-bull 28.9%) the same run printed weighted IRR 7.44% and IV@15% $68.94 — still Tier D, band D→D. The recalibration moves the size of the gap, not the verdict. Method range across defensible bases: normalized base $4.08/ADS → IV@15% $45.00; FY2024 filed-capex basis ($8.43/ADS) would roughly double the IV and still leave it far below $203.90; the maintenance definition (~$10.13/ADS for FY2024) likewise. No defensible base clears the 15% hurdle anywhere near this price.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (engine's latest FY ended 22 months ago): real limitation, named. EDGAR companyfacts has not yet ingested the FY2025 20-F (filed 2026-04-17, accession 0001193125-26-161714) — fundamentals.json carries the same warning — so the engine's history stops at FY2024. ttm.py reads us-gaap only and cannot build a TTM for this IFRS filer, so per spec the median base is used and FY2025 is handled as filing evidence instead (quoted above: OCF Ps.18,249,740 thousand, capex Ps.12,396,949 thousand, OE/share down ~34% in MXN). The FY2025 evidence points DOWN (capex ramp), so staleness is flattering the score, not penalizing it. Confidence low partly for this.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3× over 5 years): real and structural — OE is the residual after a lumpy, regulator-mandated capex program (filed capex Ps.8.4B / 10.4B / 7.8B / 12.4B across FY2022–25). ## Thoughts / verdict
This is a genuinely good asset — a regulated monopoly with 37–65% recent ROIC, a 67% EBITDA margin and a just-reset tariff — priced as if the capex that sustains it were optional. It is not: the MDP program is mandatory, the 2025–2029 cycle is bigger than the last (Ps.43,185m committed; FY2025 already spent Ps.12,397m), and FY2025 filing-basis OE/share fell ~34% in MXN on exactly that. At $203.90 the ADS offers a 2.0% normalized OE yield and a 5.56% weighted IRR; even the model's un-recalibrated, blend-driven run (weighted IRR 7.44%) and the maintenance-OE method range stay far below the 15% hurdle. The finite 2048 concession life cuts against the perpetuity terminal value the model grants it, a further reason not to stretch for the price.

**Verdict: Tier D (by numbers D, band D→D, no override). Clears Andrew's 15% hurdle only below ~$45.00 (the weighted IV@15%); the Tier A / S prices are $30.98 / $23.40.** Confidence low — data staleness (companyfacts has not ingested FY2025), FX conversion, and an override-built (but filing-sourced) base — but the verdict's direction is robust: every scenario, every base definition, and the un-recalibrated run all land in Tier D.
